title: Seeing Heat: Infrared and Webb
objective: After this level you can explain why infrared light reveals hidden and very distant objects.
summary: Infrared passes through dust and catches the stretched light of the first galaxies. Webb, launched in 2021, is built for it.

cards.headline: The newest great telescope sees in heat.
cards.body: Your skin already knows this kind of light. Hold your hand near a warm stove and you're feeling it. Now imagine a telescope built to catch it from across the universe.

cards.headline: Seeing through dust
cards.body: Infrared is the light you feel as heat. Its big trick: it passes through clouds of dust that block visible light, revealing stars forming inside them. Think of a nursery with the curtains drawn, and infrared lets you peek in. There's a second prize. Light from the most distant galaxies has been stretched by the expanding universe into infrared. To see that far away, you need a pair of infrared eyes.

cards.headline: The James Webb Space Telescope
cards.body: Earth's atmosphere blocks much infrared (Level 34), so this infrared telescope works from space. Webb launched on December 25, 2021: quite a Christmas present. Its main mirror is 6.5 meters across, made of 18 gold-coated segments. It orbits the Sun far from Earth, behind a five-layer sunshield about the size of a tennis court that keeps it extremely cold. A telescope that sees heat, parked in the shade.

cards.headline: Infrared: unveiled
learned: Infrared is light we feel as heat
It reveals stars forming inside dust
Distant galaxies’ light is stretched into infrared

questions.prompt: What kind of light is the James Webb Space Telescope built to see?

options.label: Radio waves
options.rationale: That’s the job of radio dishes.

options.label: X-rays
options.rationale: X-ray telescopes like Chandra do that.

questions.explanation: Webb is an infrared telescope, built to see through dust and to catch the stretched light of distant galaxies.

questions.prompt: Why is infrared ideal for watching stars being born?

options.label: Infrared passes through the dust clouds where stars form
Newborn stars give off only infrared light
options.rationale: They give off many kinds of light.

options.label: Infrared travels faster than visible light
options.rationale: All light travels at the same speed.

options.label: Dust clouds are brighter in ultraviolet
options.rationale: The point is to see through the dust.

questions.explanation: Stars form inside dusty clouds that block visible light. Infrared passes through that dust.

questions.prompt: From Level 34: why does it help that Webb works in space?

options.label: It can repair itself more easily there
Much infrared light never reaches the ground
Infrared light only exists in space
options.rationale: Infrared exists everywhere, even as heat on Earth.

options.label: It is closer to the distant galaxies
options.rationale: A million km is nothing on galactic scales.

questions.explanation: Earth’s atmosphere blocks much infrared light, so an infrared telescope does its best work in space.
